_description: Verified chemistry reaction data for simulation generation. The LLM should reference this data when generating chemistry practical simulations to ensure scientific accuracy.
_usage: When generating a chemistry simulation, look up the relevant reactions in this library. Use the correct equations, colors, observations, apparatus, and safety notes.

acid_base_titration.name: Acid-Base Titration

procedure.title: Fill the burette
procedure.description: Rinse the burette with NaOH solution, then fill it to the 0.00 ml mark. Remove air bubbles from the tip.

procedure.title: Measure acid sample
procedure.description: Use the pipette to transfer exactly 25.0 ml of dilute HCl into the conical flask.

procedure.title: Add indicator
procedure.description: Add 2-3 drops of phenolphthalein indicator to the HCl in the flask. The solution remains colourless.
procedure.observation: Solution remains colourless
procedure.inference: HCl is acidic — phenolphthalein is colourless in acid

procedure.title: Titrate
procedure.description: Add NaOH from the burette while swirling the flask. Start fast, then slow down near the endpoint.
procedure.observation: Solution turns pale pink at the endpoint
procedure.inference: All HCl has been neutralized by NaOH

procedure.title: Record the reading
procedure.description: Record the final burette reading. Calculate the volume of NaOH used.
procedure.observation: Burette reading gives volume of NaOH used
procedure.inference: Volume of NaOH allows calculation of unknown HCl concentration

safetyNotes: NaOH is corrosive — avoid skin contact
HCl is corrosive — handle with care
Wear safety goggles throughout
conclusionQuestions: What is the concentration of the HCl?
Why is phenolphthalein used instead of methyl orange?
What would happen if you overshoot the endpoint?

preparation_of_oxygen.name: Preparation of Oxygen Gas

procedure.title: Set up apparatus
procedure.description: Set up the delivery tube through the stopper in the test tube. Fill the trough with water and invert the gas jar filled with water over the trough.

procedure.title: Heat the KMnO₄
procedure.description: Gently heat the test tube containing KMnO₄ crystals using a Bunsen burner.
procedure.observation: Dark purple crystals produce a colourless gas. Bubbles seen collecting in the inverted gas jar.
procedure.inference: Oxygen gas is being produced and collected by downward displacement of water

procedure.title: Test for oxygen
procedure.description: When the jar is full, cover it with a glass plate and remove from water. Insert a glowing splint into the jar.

test.result: The glowing splint relights with a bright flame
test.inference: The gas is oxygen — it supports combustion

safetyNotes: KMnO₄ stains skin and clothes — wear gloves
Hot test tube — use tongs
Bunsen burner flame — tie back hair, roll up sleeves
conclusionQuestions: Why is oxygen collected by downward displacement of water?
What is the residue left in the test tube?
Write the word equation for the reaction.

preparation_of_hydrogen.name: Preparation of Hydrogen Gas

procedure.title: Set up apparatus
procedure.description: Place zinc granules in the test tube. Set up the delivery tube through the stopper into the trough of water with an inverted gas jar.

procedure.title: Add dilute HCl
procedure.description: Pour dilute hydrochloric acid through the thistle funnel onto the zinc granules.
procedure.observation: Effervescence observed. Colourless gas collected in the inverted jar by downward displacement of water.
procedure.inference: Zinc displaces hydrogen from the acid. Hydrogen is insoluble in water.

procedure.title: Test for hydrogen
procedure.description: Bring a burning splint near the mouth of the gas jar.

test.inference: The gas is hydrogen — it burns explosively with a 'pop' sound

safetyNotes: Hydrogen is flammable — keep away from naked flames
Dilute HCl is corrosive — handle with care
The 'pop' test is loud — warn students before testing
conclusionQuestions: Why is hydrogen collected by downward displacement of water?
What type of reaction is this?
Write the word equation.

preparation_of_co2.name: Preparation of Carbon Dioxide Gas

procedure.title: Set up apparatus
procedure.description: Place marble chips in the conical flask. Set up the thistle funnel and delivery tube.

procedure.title: Add acid
procedure.description: Pour dilute HCl through the thistle funnel onto the marble chips.
procedure.observation: Effervescence. Colourless gas collected by upward displacement of air.
procedure.inference: Carbon dioxide is produced. It is denser than air and slightly soluble in water.

procedure.title: Test for CO₂
procedure.description: Bubble the gas through limewater in a test tube.

test.inference: The gas is carbon dioxide — it forms insoluble CaCO₃ with limewater

safetyNotes: Dilute HCl is corrosive
CO₂ in high concentrations can cause suffocation — work in ventilated area
conclusionQuestions: Why is CO₂ collected by upward displacement of air?
Write the equation for the limewater test.
What happens when excess CO₂ is bubbled through limewater?

separation_filtration.name: Filtration — Separation of Insoluble Solid from Liquid

procedure.title: Prepare filter paper
procedure.description: Fold filter paper into a cone shape. Place it in the funnel.

procedure.title: Pour the mixture
procedure.description: Pour the sand-water mixture through the filter paper using a glass rod to guide the flow.
procedure.observation: Clear water passes through the filter paper. Sand is trapped on the paper.
procedure.inference: Insoluble solids cannot pass through the microscopic pores of filter paper

procedure.title: Collect filtrate
procedure.description: The clear liquid (filtrate) collects in the conical flask below.
procedure.observation: Filtrate is clear and colourless
procedure.inference: Filtration successfully separates insoluble solid from liquid

safetyNotes: Handle glassware carefully — broken glass is sharp
conclusionQuestions: Why do we use a glass rod when pouring?
What would happen if the filter paper had a hole?
Give an example of filtration in daily life.

separation_distillation.name: Simple Distillation — Separation of Soluble Solid from Liquid

procedure.title: Set up apparatus
procedure.description: Set up the round-bottom flask on a tripod with gauze. Connect the condenser. Place thermometer in position.

procedure.title: Heat the solution
procedure.description: Add anti-bumping granules and heat the salt water solution gently.
procedure.observation: Water boils at 100°C. Steam rises and condenses in the condenser.
procedure.inference: Water evaporates, leaving salt behind. Steam condenses back to pure water.

procedure.title: Collect distillate
procedure.description: Collect the pure water (distillate) in the beaker.
procedure.observation: Clear, colourless liquid collects. White solid residue left in the flask.
procedure.inference: Distillation separates a soluble solid from water. The distillate is pure water.

safetyNotes: Hot apparatus — use tongs
Anti-bumping granules prevent violent boiling
conclusionQuestions: Why is the thermometer bulb placed at the side arm of the flask?
What is the residue left in the flask?
How could you test the distillate is pure water?

flame_tests.name: Flame Tests for Metal Ions

procedure.title: Clean the wire
procedure.description: Dip the platinum wire in dilute HCl and hold it in the blue Bunsen flame until no colour change.
procedure.observation: Wire glows but no colour change in the flame
procedure.inference: Wire is clean — HCl removes impurities

procedure.title: Test sodium
procedure.description: Dip the wire in NaCl solution, then hold it in the flame.
procedure.observation: Flame turns intense yellow/orange
procedure.inference: Yellow flame = Sodium ions (Na⁺)

procedure.title: Test potassium
procedure.description: Clean the wire, dip in KCl solution, hold in the flame. View through blue cobalt glass.
procedure.observation: Flame turns lilac/pale purple
procedure.inference: Lilac flame = Potassium ions (K⁺). Blue glass filters out yellow sodium light.

procedure.title: Test calcium
procedure.description: Clean the wire, dip in CaCl₂ solution, hold in the flame.
procedure.observation: Flame turns brick red/orange-red
procedure.inference: Brick red flame = Calcium ions (Ca²⁺)

procedure.title: Test copper
procedure.description: Clean the wire, dip in CuSO₄ solution, hold in the flame.
procedure.observation: Flame turns green/blue-green
procedure.inference: Green flame = Copper(II) ions (Cu²⁺)

safetyNotes: Platinum wire gets very hot — use tongs
Bunsen burner flame — tie back hair
HCl is corrosive
conclusionQuestions: Why must the wire be cleaned with HCl before each test?
Why is blue cobalt glass used for the potassium test?
How could you identify an unknown salt using flame tests?

acid_reactions.name: Reactions of Acids

procedure.title: Acid + Metal
procedure.description: Add dilute HCl to magnesium ribbon in a test tube.
procedure.observation: Effervescence. Colourless gas collected. Test tube becomes hot.
procedure.inference: Magnesium displaces hydrogen from the acid. Reaction is exothermic.

procedure.title: Acid + Metal Oxide
procedure.description: Add dilute HCl to black copper(II) oxide powder.
procedure.observation: Black powder dissolves. Blue/green solution forms.
procedure.inference: CuO is a basic oxide — it reacts with acid to form salt and water (neutralization).

procedure.title: Acid + Carbonate
procedure.description: Add dilute HCl to sodium carbonate powder.
procedure.observation: Effervescence. Gas turns limewater milky.
procedure.inference: Carbonates react with acid to produce carbon dioxide gas.

safetyNotes: Acids are corrosive — wear goggles and gloves
Hydrogen is flammable
CO₂ in large amounts can cause drowsiness
conclusionQuestions: What do all acid + metal reactions produce?
How do you know the gas from step 3 is CO₂?
Write the general word equation: Acid + Metal Oxide → ?

displacement_reactions.name: Displacement Reactions with Metals

procedure.title: Iron in copper sulphate
procedure.description: Place an iron nail in copper(II) sulphate solution.
procedure.observation: Brown/reddish copper deposits on the iron nail. Blue solution turns green.
procedure.inference: Iron is more reactive than copper — it displaces copper from its salt solution.

procedure.title: Copper in zinc sulphate
procedure.description: Place a copper strip in zinc sulphate solution.
procedure.observation: No visible change.
procedure.inference: Copper is less reactive than zinc — it cannot displace zinc.

safetyNotes: Copper sulphate is harmful — avoid skin contact
Wash hands after handling metal solutions
conclusionQuestions: Which metal is more reactive: iron or copper?
Write the word equation for step 1.
Predict what would happen if you placed zinc in copper sulphate solution.

rate_of_reaction.name: Factors Affecting Rate of Reaction

procedure.title: Effect of concentration
procedure.description: React 5g marble chips with 50ml of HCl at different concentrations (0.5M, 1.0M, 2.0M). Measure volume of CO₂ collected in 30 seconds.
procedure.observation: Higher concentration → faster effervescence → more gas collected in 30s
procedure.inference: Higher concentration increases frequency of collisions between reactant particles

procedure.title: Effect of surface area
procedure.description: Compare reaction rate using marble chips vs marble powder with the same concentration of HCl.
procedure.observation: Marble powder reacts faster than marble chips
procedure.inference: Greater surface area increases frequency of collisions

procedure.title: Effect of temperature
procedure.description: React at room temperature vs 40°C vs 60°C using a water bath.
procedure.observation: Higher temperature → faster reaction
procedure.inference: Higher temperature increases kinetic energy and frequency of successful collisions

safetyNotes: HCl is corrosive
Hot water bath — use tongs
MnO₂ is an irritant — avoid inhaling dust
conclusionQuestions: Draw a graph of volume of gas vs time for different concentrations.
Explain in terms of collision theory why higher temperature increases rate.
What is the role of MnO₂ in hydrogen peroxide decomposition?
